The paragraph opens 'In philosophical alchemy, salt is a cosmic principle... it is correlated with the feminine, lunar side' — reported doctrine of the tradition, not Jung's own claim.
'It was called the prima materia of Sol, Sol being naturally understood as the gold' reports alchemical usage ('was called', 'understood as'), not Jung's interpretive voice.
'Luna also signifies silver' is presented amid 'the statements of the alchemists about Luna' — reported alchemical terminology, not Jung's own assertion.
'Sulphur is one of the innumerable synonyms for the prima materia' summarizes footnoted alchemical usage ('it was called', 'is said') — reported doctrine of the tradition.
The paragraph states 'In alchemy the lion... is a synonym for Mercurius' — explicitly attributed to the alchemical tradition, not Jung's own interpretive claim.
The lion taking the king's place is the content of the 'lion hunt' of Marchos allegory that Jung is recounting, not a claim in his own voice.
Beya causing Gabricus to disappear into her body is the narrative of the Arisleus vision, which Jung recounts as a parallel rather than asserts himself.
'The whore (meretrix) is a well-known figure in alchemy' — the meretrix characterization of the arcane substance is reported alchemical doctrine backed by treatise quotations.
The Moor/Ethiopian as the black, sinful man is presented as patristic and alchemical symbolism (St. Hilary, Chymical Wedding, Mylius), which Jung reports rather than asserts.
'The alchemists therefore pictured the unio mentalis as Father and Son and their union as the dove' — explicitly the alchemists' picturing, reported by Jung.
The paragraph attributes the stage doctrine explicitly: 'in Dorn's view a mental union was... merely the first stage' — Dorn's doctrine reported, not Jung's own assertion.
The second-stage conjunction with the body belongs to the same Dorn stage-sequence framed by 'in Dorn's view' — reported doctrine, not Jung's own assertion.
'Mercurius, it is generally affirmed, is the arcanum, the prima materia' rests on anonymous general alchemical affirmation, not a quoted named source, so quotes-source with 'alchemists' is wrong.

The edge rests on 'the apparently absurd statement of the alchemists' — generic reported doctrine, not a quoted named source, so quotes-source is the wrong type.
The claim is explicitly hedged — 'Presumably the leftward circumambulation... indicates that the squaring of the circle is a stage on the way to the unconscious' — so confidence should be medium.
'Thus we hear that the vas is the water... the Mercurius of the philosophers' rests on unnamed texts ('we hear that'), so it is reported tradition, not a quoted named source.
Adam as symbol of the prima materia is the alchemists' own usage ('he called his prima materia Adam', Turba and Gabir quoted); Jung reports and explains it rather than asserting it.
